STAFFING SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Staffing Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is made as of February 2, 2026 between Rothesay Analytics Corp., a Massachusetts corporation ("Client"), and Larkspur Talent Partners LLC, a Massachusetts limited liability company ("Supplier").

1. SERVICES

1.1 Assignment of Personnel. Supplier shall furnish qualified personnel ("Assigned Personnel") to perform the services described in each work order the parties execute under this Agreement (each a "Work Order"). Each Work Order shall state the role, the required skills, the location, the anticipated duration, the bill rate, and any Client-specific onboarding requirements.

1.2 Recruiting and Screening. Supplier shall recruit, interview, and screen candidates, verify employment eligibility on Form I-9, confirm licensure where required, and, where the Work Order specifies and applicable law permits, conduct background checks and drug screening in compliance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act and applicable state law.

1.3 Replacement. If Client determines within the first ten (10) business days of an assignment that an individual is not performing satisfactorily, Client may request replacement, and Supplier shall not charge for the hours worked by that individual during that period.

2. EMPLOYMENT RELATIONSHIP

2.1 Supplier Is the Employer. Assigned Personnel are employees of Supplier and are not employees of Client for any purpose. Supplier is solely responsible for hiring, discipline, termination, wages, overtime, bonuses, benefits, payroll taxes, unemployment insurance, and workers' compensation coverage for Assigned Personnel, and shall pay all of them when due.

2.2 No Co-Employment. Client does not control the manner or means by which Supplier discharges its employer obligations. Client shall not administer discipline, set wage rates, or make hiring or termination decisions for Assigned Personnel, and shall direct any performance concern to Supplier's account manager. Nothing in this Agreement makes Client a joint employer of any Assigned Personnel, and neither party intends that result.

2.3 Benefits Waiver. Assigned Personnel are not eligible to participate in any employee benefit plan of Client, and Supplier shall obtain from each Assigned Person a written acknowledgment of that fact before the assignment begins. If a court or agency nevertheless determines that an Assigned Person is a common-law employee of Client, that person remains ineligible for Client's benefit plans, and Supplier shall indemnify Client for any resulting benefit liability.

2.4 Wage and Hour. Supplier shall classify each Assigned Person correctly under the Fair Labor Standards Act and applicable state law, shall pay overtime as required, and shall maintain accurate time records. Client shall approve time records weekly and shall not request or permit off-the-clock work.

3. FEES AND INVOICING

3.1 Bill Rates. Client shall pay the bill rates stated in each Work Order. Bill rates are inclusive of wages, statutory burden, benefits, insurance, and Supplier's margin, and no other charge applies unless the Work Order states it.

3.2 Overtime. Hours worked in excess of forty (40) in a workweek are billed at one and one-half times the straight-time bill rate.

3.3 Invoicing and Payment. Supplier shall invoice weekly in arrears with supporting time records. Client shall pay each undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days after receipt. Client may withhold a disputed amount if it notifies Supplier within ten (10) days after receiving the invoice, and shall pay the undisputed balance.

3.4 Conversion. Client may hire an Assigned Person as its own employee after that person has completed one thousand (1,000) hours on assignment at no fee. Before that threshold, Client shall pay a conversion fee equal to fifteen percent (15%) of the person's annualized base salary, declining by one percent (1%) for each 100 hours worked on assignment.

3.5 No Markup on Pass-Through. Supplier shall not mark up any expense reimbursed by Client and shall pass through such expenses at cost with documentation.

4. COMPLIANCE

4.1 Equal Opportunity and Anti-Harassment. Each party shall comply with Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Americans with Disabilities Act, the Age Discrimination in Employment Act, and applicable state and local law. Supplier shall train Assigned Personnel on anti-harassment as Massachusetts law requires, and Client shall extend its anti-harassment reporting channels to Assigned Personnel working at its sites.

4.2 Immigration. Supplier shall verify the employment eligibility of each Assigned Person and shall retain Form I-9 documentation as required.

4.3 Safety. Client shall provide a workplace that complies with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, shall provide site-specific safety training and any required personal protective equipment, and shall report any injury to an Assigned Person to Supplier within twenty-four (24) hours.

4.4 Confidentiality and Data. Supplier shall cause each Assigned Person to execute Client's standard confidentiality and invention-assignment agreement before the assignment begins. Supplier shall comply with Client's information-security requirements when handling Client data.

5. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

5.1 Work Product. All right, title, and interest in and to any work product, invention, or work of authorship created by an Assigned Person in the course of an assignment vests in Client. Supplier assigns, and shall cause each Assigned Person to assign, all such right, title, and interest to Client, and shall execute any document reasonably required to perfect or record the assignment.

6. INDEMNITY, INSURANCE, AND LIABILITY

6.1 Supplier Indemnity. Supplier shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Client against any claim arising out of Supplier's breach of this Agreement, its failure to pay wages, taxes, or benefits, its misclassification of an Assigned Person, or any employment claim brought by an Assigned Person against Client that arises from Supplier's acts or omissions.

6.2 Client Indemnity. Client shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Supplier against any claim arising out of Client's breach of this Agreement, unsafe conditions at Client's site, or Client's direction of an Assigned Person outside the scope of the applicable Work Order.

6.3 Procedure. The indemnified party shall give prompt written notice, the indemnifying party shall control the defense with counsel reasonably acceptable to the indemnified party, and no settlement imposing a non-monetary obligation on the indemnified party may be made without its consent.

6.4 Insurance. Supplier shall maintain workers' compensation as required by law with employer's liability of $1,000,000, commercial general liability of $2,000,000 per occurrence, employment practices liability of $2,000,000, professional liability of $2,000,000, and a fidelity bond of $500,000, and shall name Client as an additional insured on the general liability policy.

6.5 Limitation of Liability. Except for the indemnity obligations in Section 6, breach of Section 4.4, and a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, neither party's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall exceed the fees paid or payable under the applicable Work Order in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, and neither party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages.

7. TERM AND TERMINATION

7.1 Term. This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for two (2) years, renewing for successive one-year terms unless either party gives sixty (60) days' written notice of non-renewal.

7.2 Termination. Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience on thirty (30) days' written notice, and either party may terminate immediately if the other materially breaches and fails to cure within fifteen (15) days after written notice. Client may end any individual assignment at any time on notice to Supplier.

7.3 Effect of Termination. Termination of this Agreement does not affect any Work Order in progress unless the terminating party states otherwise, and Client shall pay for all hours worked through the effective date of termination. Sections 2, 4.4, 5, 6 and 8 survive.

8. GENERAL

8.1 Governing Law; Venue. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. Any action arising out of this Agreement shall be brought in the state or federal courts located in Suffolk County, Massachusetts.

8.2 Non-Solicitation. During the term and for twelve (12) months after it, neither party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other who was directly involved in the services, except that a general advertisement not targeted at those employees is permitted.

8.3 Assignment. Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other's written consent, except to a successor to substantially all of its business.

8.4 Notices. All notices shall be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by electronic mail with confirmation of receipt, to the addresses stated beneath the signatures.

8.5 Entire Agreement; Amendment. This Agreement, with its Work Orders, is the entire agreement between the parties and may be amended only in a writing signed by both.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the date first written above.

ROTHESAY ANALYTICS CORP.
